cases.sentence: Два раза переменив лошадей и в полтора часа проскакав 30 верст по грязной ___, Болховитинов во втором часу ночи был в Леташевке.
cases.explain: «вязкой дороге» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: It was a warm, dark, autumn night. It had been raining for four days. Having changed horses twice and galloped twenty miles in an hour and a half over a sticky, muddy road, Bolkhovítinov reached Litashëvka after one o’clock at night. Dismounting at a cottage on whose wattle fence hung a signboard, general staff, and throwing down his reins, he entered a dark passage.

cases.explain: «Дежурного генерала» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “The general on duty, quick! It’s very important!” said he to someone who had risen and was sniffing in the dark passage.

cases.sentence: — С вечера нездоровы очень были, третью ночь не спят, — заступнически прошептал ___.
cases.explain: «денщицкий голос» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “He has been very unwell since the evening and this is the third night he has not slept,” said the orderly pleadingly in a whisper. “You should wake the captain first.”

cases.explain: «сонный голос» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Your honor, your honor! A courier.” “What? What’s that? From whom?” came a sleepy voice.

cases.sentence: Когда сначала синим и потом ___ загорелись серники о трут, Щербинин зажег сальную свечку, с подсвечника которой побежали обгладывавшие ее прусаки, и осмотрел вестника.
cases.explain: «красным пламенем» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: When the flame of the sulphur splinters kindled by the tinder burned up, first blue and then red, Shcherbínin lit the tallow candle, from the candlestick of which the cockroaches that had been gnawing it were running away, and looked at the messenger. Bolkhovítinov was bespattered all over with mud and had smeared his face by wiping it with his sleeve.

cases.sentence: — Нечего делать, надо будить, — сказал Щербинин, вставая и подходя к человеку в ___, укрытому шинелью; — Петр Петрович!
cases.explain: «ночном колпаке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “There’s nothing to be done, we’ll have to wake him,” said Shcherbínin, rising and going up to the man in the nightcap who lay covered by a greatcoat. “Pyotr Petróvich!” said he.

cases.sentence: И действительно, голова в ___ поднялась тотчас же.
cases.explain: «ночном колпаке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: (Konovnítsyn did not stir.) “To the General Staff!” he said with a smile, knowing that those words would be sure to arouse him. And in fact the head in the nightcap was lifted at once. On Konovnítsyn’s handsome, resolute face with cheeks flushed by fever, there still remained for an instant a faraway dreamy expression remote from present affairs, but then he suddenly started and his face assumed its habitual calm and firm appearance.

cases.sentence: Едва прочтя, он опустил ноги в ___ на земляной пол и стал обуваться.
cases.explain: «шерстяных чулках» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Well, what is it? From whom?” he asked immediately but without hurry, blinking at the light. While listening to the officer’s report Konovnítsyn broke the seal and read the dispatch. Hardly had he done so before he lowered his legs in their woolen stockings to the earthen floor and began putting on his boots. Then he took off his nightcap, combed his hair over his temples, and donned his cap.
